The Taihang strip of 185-205 (Heishan confederacy) is carried here at confidence 1 on the Zhang Yan page's 'raised forces during the Yellow Turban revolt'; the Heishan bandits page calls the founders 'unrelated to the Yellow Turban movement', so a separate bandit entry would be the cleaner home (gap noted).

capitals.note: The rebel base the page names is Julu-Wei; Guangzong is where Lu Zhi besieged Zhang Jue; coordinates are the modern county seat, approximate.

keyframe_review.note: Reviewer fix (ea-02-x-fixed): the Xuchang circle (Runan-Yingchuan) is dropped from the held shape because the ledger only opens and closes a contest there (/ledger/2-3) and the page has Bo Cai fighting, not holding: 'Sometime between 28 May and 25 June, Zhu Jun, Huangfu Song, and Cao Cao joined forces to defeat Bo Cai at Changshe'. Nanyang is now lost in the ledger (185/1); both centres are lost in January 185, so this keyframe ends with 184 and the Taihang shape starts in 185. The page names the places, not a frontier; the body names four provinces ('mostly concentrated in the Ji, Jing, You and Yu provinces'), the eight only in a Chinese footnote. Rendered as a rebel hatch.

correction.text: the Taihang Mountains, where the Heishan bandits 'operated as a bandit confederacy' with access to Henei and the provinces of Bing, Ji and Yan

keyframe_review.note: Reviewer fix (ea-02-x-fixed): the three Taihang keyframes (186-187, 188-192, 193-205) are merged into one because Shandong (admin1) is dropped from 188-192: the page has Qing and Xu rebels who 'resurged' and raided, not a held province, so Qing, Xu and Yan are the contest zone of /ledger 188/11-192/5 only. CONFIDENCE 1 SHAPE: the Taihang strip is a placeholder for the Heishan confederacy ('operated as a bandit confederacy in the Taihang Mountains', access to 'Henei and the provinces of Bing, Ji, and Yan', raid on Julu in 185). The Heishan page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heishan_bandits) adds raids on Changshan, Zhao, Zhongshan, Shangdang and Henei and says the founders were 'unrelated to the Yellow Turban movement'; the Zhang Yan page says only that he 'raised forces during the Yellow Turban revolt'. The strip is carried in this dossier on the Zhang Yan page's wording and the rebellion page's end year (205), not as a claim that the Heishan were Yellow Turbans. yuan-shao takes this circle out of its Ji Province for 191-204, so the ground is held once.

region.text: Zhang Jue's base: 'Julu and Wei commanderies' of Ji Province, followers told to gather at Ye

ledger.note: 184: Zhang Jue raises the Yellow Turbans. 'In March, Zhang Jue started the Yellow Turban Rebellion with roughly 360,000 followers' (proclaimed 4 March); he was 'based in Julu and Wei commanderies' of Ji Province, followers to gather at Ye.

region.text: Wancheng in Nanyang Commandery, seized by Zhang Mancheng on 24 March 184

ledger.note: 184: Wancheng falls to the rebels. Zhang Mancheng seized Wancheng (Nanyang Commandery, Jing Province) on 24 March 184; Zhang Mancheng was killed between 26 June and 25 July 184 and Zhao Hong took over at Wancheng, which imperial forces retook by the beginning of 185 (see the 185 loss).

region.text: Runan and Yingchuan, where Bo Cai's rebels fought at Changshe (28 May to 25 June 184)

ledger.note: 184: the Yu Province front. Bo Cai's rebels fought at Changshe between 28 May and 25 June 184, then at Yangzhai and Xihua (Runan and Yingchuan). The page says they fought there, not that they held it.

region.text: Runan and Yingchuan, where Bo Cai's rebels fought at Changshe (28 May to 25 June 184)

ledger.note: 184: Bo Cai and Peng Tuo are defeated at Yangzhai and Xihua (no dates on the page; month 6 is the end of the page's Changshe window, 25 June); the Yu Province front is closed within the year.

region.text: the Taihang Mountains, where the Heishan bandits 'operated as a bandit confederacy' with access to Henei and the provinces of Bing, Ji and Yan

ledger.note: 185: PAGE SILENT on when the Heishan took any ground. The Zhang Yan page has the confederacy 'in the Taihang Mountains' raiding Julu Commandery 'in 185'; the Taihang strip is entered from that year as a placeholder (confidence 1). The Heishan page calls the founders 'unrelated to the Yellow Turban movement': this dossier carries the strip because the Zhang Yan page says he 'raised forces during the Yellow Turban revolt', not on any page that calls the Heishan Yellow Turbans.

region.text: Zhang Jue's base: 'Julu and Wei commanderies' of Ji Province, followers told to gather at Ye

ledger.note: 185: the Ji Province core is lost. Zhang Jue died of illness in October 184, Zhang Liang was killed at Guangzong between 21 November and 20 December 184 and Zhang Bao at Xiaquyang between 21 December 184 and 18 January 185; 'main fighting ended by February 185' (the page's range spans the year line, so 185 month 1 is used).

region.text: Wancheng in Nanyang Commandery, seized by Zhang Mancheng on 24 March 184

ledger.note: 185: Wancheng is retaken. 'By the beginning of 185, the rebellion had mostly been suppressed following Zhu Jun's recapture of Wancheng in Nanyang Commandery'; the page dates neither the recapture nor Zhao Hong's last stand (Zhao Hong, who succeeded Zhang Mancheng, was killed 'during or after October 184'), so 185 month 1, the page's 'beginning of 185', is the ceiling date.

region.text: Qing and Xu Provinces, where the rebels 'resurged' from about November 188, and Yan Province, entered about May 192

ledger.note: 188: the Yellow Turbans rise again in Qing and Xu. 'Qing and Xu Provinces: rebels resurged around November 188'; Zhang Rao raided Qing about 189; the Guo Tai rebels of Xihe (March-April 188) became the White Wave Bandits.

region.text: Qing and Xu Provinces, where the rebels 'resurged' from about November 188, and Yan Province, entered about May 192

ledger.note: 192: the Qing rebels move on Yan and are broken. 'Around May 192, hundreds of thousands of Yellow Turban remnants from Qing Province swarmed into Yan Province'; Cao Cao then defeated them in Jibei State and the rebels, 'numbering over 300,000, surrendered' (the page dates the surrender no closer than 'later', so the contest is closed at 192 without a month; the earlier note's 'Around May 192, over 300,000 rebels surrendered' joined two sentences). Cao Cao formed the Qingzhou Army from their best warriors.

region.text: the Taihang Mountains, where the Heishan bandits 'operated as a bandit confederacy' with access to Henei and the provinces of Bing, Ji and Yan

ledger.note: 205: the last Yellow Turban remnant submits. 'In summer 205 he surrendered with 100,000 followers' (Zhang Yan, Heishan); the rebellion page: 'By the year 205 (21 years after it had begun) the Yellow Turban Rebellion was over.' The Taihang land passes to Cao Cao.

notes:
Yellow Turbans, rebel state (type rebel). Cliopatria has no row; its Han shape 184-196 keeps the whole empire (ea-02-c han-dynasty_184 ok). 3 pages opened (Yellow Turban Rebellion; Zhang Yan (Han dynasty); Heishan bandits, added in the repair pass), within the 2-5 page budget for a state without a Cliopatria row.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): (1) Nanyang is now lost in the ledger (185/1, confidence 2): the rebellion page says only 'By the beginning of 185 ... following Zhu Jun's recapture of Wancheng', with Zhao Hong killed 'during or after October 184'. (2) The Xuchang circle (Runan-Yingchuan) is out of the held shape; it stays a contest zone (/ledger/2-3, war zone). (3) The Taihang strip has a gain (185, confidence 1). The Heishan bandits page says the founders were 'unrelated to the Yellow Turban movement'; the Zhang Yan page says he 'raised forces during the Yellow Turban revolt'. The dossier keeps the strip because the rebellion page counts the rebellion to 205, but a separate Heishan entry would be cleaner. (4) Shandong is out of the 188-192 shape (raids and a contest, not a held province), so the three Taihang keyframes became one (185-205). (5) yuan-shao now carves the Taihang circle out of its Ji Province for 191-204. (6) The 192 contest_end note joined two sentences of the page; corrected, month dropped, confidence 2.
Could not settle: (1) the English pages name no frontier, so the 184 shape is two place clusters (Xiangtai/Handan for Julu-Wei, Nanyang for Wancheng), not a border; (2) the page body names four provinces (Ji, Jing, You, Yu) and lists the eight only in a Chinese footnote (Qing, Xu, You, Ji, Jing, Yang, Yan, Yu); the You front (Guo Xun, Inspector of You, and Liu Wei killed) and the Yang front (Shu County attacked) are undated and not mapped; (3) the 185-205 Taihang shape is a placeholder (confidence 1): neither the Zhang Yan nor the Heishan page gives a boundary, though the Heishan page names raids in Changshan, Zhao, Zhongshan, Shangdang and Henei; (4) no date for the Wancheng recapture or the Jibei surrender.
Counterparts: han-dynasty exists (ea-02-c); cao-cao exists (Cliopatria 197-223, ea-03). No dossier needed for Cao Cao's Qingzhou Army. Gazetteer: all names resolve (Xiangtai is Natural Earth's spelling of Xingtai/Julu region).
